title: Regional queue collapse during promotional traffic spike — fallback and circuit-safeguard action plan
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description: Summary: On 2025-02-11 we observed a sharp regional latency and error spike in us-west-2 during a large promotional traffic increase from several customers. The regional request queue for text-generation endpoints backed up, causing circuit breakers to trip unevenly across zones and a cascade of degraded tail latency for 38 minutes. The incident caused SLO misses for 15% of hosts in the region and visible 5xx spikes for a set of enterprise customers using Dedicated routing. This ticket documents the postmortem, the immediate mitigations, and a prioritized action plan to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2025-02-11T09:04:00Z - Traffic surge detected: +320% tokens/s in us-west-2 compared to baseline (promo window start).
2025-02-11T09:06:00Z - Alert: regional p50/p99 latency breach triggered (SLO: p99 < 1.2s; observed p99 ~ 3.7s).
2025-02-11T09:08:00Z - Automated circuit breakers engaged for lower-priority routes but not consistently due to stale config divergence between control plane and edge (some hosts still routing).
2025-02-11T09:12:00Z - Control plane observed queue growth; operators enabled emergency graded shedding rule to reject low-priority embeddings and batch jobs.
2025-02-11T09:18:00Z - Partial fallback to secondary region initiated for traffic tagged as 'best-effort' (about 8% of requests).
2025-02-11T09:28:00Z - Manual throttles applied to dedicated pools for affected customers; KV-cache warmup scripts executed to reduce cold-KV penalties.
2025-02-11T09:42:00Z - Traffic receded; systems recovered to baseline by 09:47. Post-incident alerting and SLO dashboards created for follow-ups.
detection: Primary detection was SLO-alerting on regional p99 latency and an operator noticing a correlated spike in 'queue_depth' and 'inflight_requests' metrics. Pager duty page was triggered by the on-call reliability engineer. Synthetic health checks did not fail because they used small, prioritized routes and therefore masked the broader queue saturation behavior.
root_cause: Three contributing factors: (1) promotional traffic pattern produced many medium-length generation requests with high token counts, shifting sequence-length distribution and defeating our default batching heuristics; (2) a control-plane config propagation lag (~45s) left stale circuit-breaker thresholds on ~20% of edge hosts, preventing coordinated shedding; (3) priority-eviction logic in the regional queue had an off-by-one bug that allowed low-priority jobs to occupy head-of-queue slots under certain timing windows, increasing head-of-line blocking.
immediate_mitigation: Enabled graded-shedding rule to reject non-critical embeddings and offline batch jobs (rolled back when stable). Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/d/us-west-2/incident-999981
Forced a coordinated circuit reset via control-plane roll (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/6212) to clear stale thresholds and re-sync host configs.
Applied emergency priority-eviction patch to regional queue manager to enforce strict prioritization (hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/8349).
Initiated targeted fallback for 'best-effort' route to secondary region (us-east-1) for 8% of eligible traffic while preserving affinity for premium customers.
impact_metrics: Affected hosts in region: 15% had p99 > 1.2s
Customer-visible 5xx increase: +0.9% absolute for the region during the window
Estimated cost of emergency fallback/egress: $4.3k for the incident window
postmortem_notes: Batching heuristics must incorporate observed token-count distribution changes instead of only request-rate heuristics—short-term patch landed to bias batch formation when median sequence length > 128 tokens.

Config propagation path audit revealed a corner-case where incremental config diffs could be dropped during transient control-plane leader elections—this must be hardened with persistent seq numbers and retry logic.
Priority-eviction bug traced to a race between queue-scan and the admission controller; we added an ordered lock and unit tests that reproduce the timing window.
Synthetic health checks will be expanded to include representative mixed-length requests (not just short priority checks) so they exercise batching and queue behavior.
Canary deployment process for control-plane config changes will be updated to include a verification step that checks circuit-breaker knobs on a sample of edge hosts before 100% rollout.

PRI-03: Fix priority-eviction race and add timing-unit tests. Owner: Sofia Martinez. Due: 2025-02-22. (Estimate: 2)
PRI-04: Expand synthetic check matrix to cover mid-length and long requests. Owner: Ethan Park. Due: 2025-03-01. (Estimate: 2)
PRI-05: Implement coordinated circuit reset tooling for emergency operator workflows (CLI + one-click in Console). Owner: Kai Morgan. Due: 2025-03-12. (Estimate: 5)
PRI-06: Create canary verification step for control-plane rollouts that samples 10% of edge hosts and asserts circuit config parity. Owner: DevOps Squad. Due: 2025-02-26. (Estimate: 3)
PRI-07: Run a chaos experiment to validate graded-shedding policies under promo-like loads. Owner: Reliability Eng. Due: 2025-03-10. (Estimate: 4)
